subject: ventures/3pl-quote-normalizer
professional: an e-commerce operations manager (or 3PL sales engineer) who normalizes competing fulfilment rate cards; first checks: storage unit conversions (pallet vs bin/shelf vs cubic foot), whether the monthly minimum includes postage, per-order vs per-unit pick fees, peak-season surcharges, long-term storage, receiving per pallet/carton/unit, and whether the in-house comparison treats fixed costs as fixed

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs from node (scratchpad r.mjs) and the live page in headless Chromium against a local static server, and recomputed by hand from rate-card arithmetic. Defaults: variable per order = receiving 1.5 x 0.12 = 0.18 + first pick 2.75 + 0.5 extra unit x 0.50 = 3.00 + packaging 0.60 + shipping 8.50 + returns 0.08 x (2.50 + 0.40) = 0.232 -> 12.512; fixed = 1 pallet x 18 + 150 = 168; total 100 x 12.512 + 168 = $1,419.20, $14.19/order (tool: 1419.20, 14.192, page hero '$1,419.20 / month'). Break-even 13N = 168 + 12.512N -> N = 344.3 -> 345 (tool 345). Minimum $2,500: total 2,500, $25/order, orders to clear on volume (2500-168)/12.512 = 186.4 -> 187 (tool 187, page shows it). Inbound $10/60-unit pallet, $1.50/6-unit carton on 150 units: 0.1667 and 0.25/unit, $25 and $37.50 (tool same). Aged storage 10 pallets, 4 leftover at $45: 6x18 + 4x45 = $288, surcharge $108, liquidation recovery 480 / hold 180 = 2.67 months (tool same). Return disposition defaults: restock 8+3.5+4+0.4 + 18x0.3 + 1.5x0.3 = $21.75, destroy $31, keep $18, restock-beats-keep unit cost 16.35/0.7 = $23.36 (tool same). Kitting: 6-2.8-4.86 = -$1.66, pre-kit $2.30 (tool same). But one displayed output is wrong: when the 3PL's variable cost per order exceeds the in-house rate (e.g. in-house $10 vs 3PL $12.51) there is no break-even, the engine knows it (breakEvenFound false), yet the summary prints 'Break-even volume: about 0 orders/month' (calc.mjs:960), the page shows '0 orders' (index.html:125 render) and the CSV/JSON export writes 0 (export.mjs:28,52). 0 is also what the tool prints when the 3PL wins at every volume (found true, orders 0), so the same figure means opposite things. Also, after a reload the page silently resets the return-handling fee to $2.50 (observed in Chromium: typed 5, total $1,439.20; after reload field 2.5, total $1,419.20). Arithmetic right on 9 of 10 recomputed outputs, one shown output wrong, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README feature end to end: normalized monthly total, cost per order, searched break-even, minimum-spend handling and orders-to-clear (all run); two-quote compare page, target budget, CSV/JSON export, share link, copy summary, volume sensitivity, returns sensitivity, long-term storage, return disposition, kitting, inbound method, cost drivers and negotiation brief pages all present, linked and backed by exported calc.mjs functions with tests (136 tests). Blank/negative/non-numeric input warnings work (calculate({orders:'-5',shipping:'abc',pallets:''}) returns three explicit warnings). served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin. Gap: the return-fee and restock-fee inputs the README says the calculator exposes are injected by return-fields.js on DOMContentLoaded, after the module script has already restored saved values, so a saved custom value is not restored. README Development command lists 2 of 9 test files.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject dir: 136 pass, 0 fail, ~0.5 s. Seven seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: additional-pick formula, restock fee dropped from returns, monthly minimum added instead of max(), pallet inbound rate halved, destroy-leftover term zeroed, long-term surcharge not net of base rate: all caught. Orders-to-clear-minimum ignoring storage and fixed fees (calc.mjs:39) SURVIVED: tests only assert the line 'clear the minimum' appears. No test checks what the UI or export shows when breakEvenFound is false, and no browser test covers the return-fee field restore.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (975 lines), index.html (one 1-line inline module script of several KB), return-fields.js, export.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Defects: return-fee inputs added by a separate classic script on DOMContentLoaded race the module that restores localStorage (verified in Chromium); defaults for the same field differ by function (receivingPerUnit 0.12 in calculate vs 0.45 in inboundReceivingPerUnit, calc.mjs:156; returnFee 2.5/restockFee 0.4 in calculate vs 3.5/4 in compareReturnDisposition, calc.mjs:532-533); two copies of the number-parsing helper (calc.mjs:2 and :333); five near-identical try/catch render-error blocks in index.html; breakEvenFound computed but never consumed by any renderer. Engine is pure and exported, tests import the shipped module.
evidence.claims: Checked: disclaimer and no-warranty on all 15 HTML pages (grep -L 'No warranty' *.html empty); no network calls (no fetch/sendBeacon/XMLHttpRequest in any file); pallet-vs-carton page '$80 vs $120 vs $192, $112 gap on 480 units' recomputes (8 pallets x 10, 80 cartons x 1.5, 480 x 0.40); kitting page '-$1.66 per kit, pre-kit $2.30, beats skip at $1.84 kit fee or $7.66 lift' recomputes; restock page '$23.36' recomputes; vs-ShipBob and vs-Extensiv state no competitor price and disclaim affiliation; sitemap lists all 15 pages. Weak: kitting page calls its defaults 'typical' with no source; README 'Development' test command is stale. The FAQ honestly warns that an in-house rate missing rent makes break-even wrong.
evidence.fitness: Walked an ops manager's job: type a 3PL rate card, get monthly all-in and cost per order, compare to in-house, see the minimum's effect, compare a second provider. The single-quote job finishes for a pallet-priced card. It stalls on common cards: storage only per pallet (no bin/shelf/cubic-foot line or conversion, which ShipBob-style and many 3PL cards use); no peak-season surcharge; no per-SKU, account-setup or onboarding fees; the minimum is applied to a subtotal that includes postage, with no option for minimums on fulfilment fees only; the compare page takes only two pre-normalized totals, so the second quote must be normalized separately; pallets stay constant while the sensitivity sweep runs 25 to 500 orders.
evidence.domain: Per-order plus additional-unit picks, receiving converted from pallet/carton to per unit, minimum as max(subtotal, floor), and returns at rate x (handling + restock) match how fulfilment rate cards are built. Departures a practitioner would flag: in-house cost is a single per-order rate held constant while the searched break-even re-prices the 3PL across volumes, so in-house fixed costs (rent, staff, WMS) that the FAQ tells the user to fold into that rate are treated as variable, inverting the usual outsourcing break-even shape (3PL cheaper at low volume); minimums usually exclude postage at many 3PLs and the tool cannot model that; inbound pallets/cartons are charged fractionally (150 units / 60 = 2.5 pallets) rather than per whole container; long-term storage is modelled as a replacement rate, while many cards bill it on top of base storage; no peak surcharge or cubic-foot storage.

defects.what: When no break-even exists (3PL variable cost per order above the in-house rate, e.g. in-house $10 vs $12.51), the engine sets breakEvenFound false but the summary prints 'Break-even volume: about 0 orders/month', the page shows '0 orders' and the CSV/JSON export writes 0; 0 is also printed when the 3PL wins at every volume, so the same figure means opposite decisions

Saved return-handling and restock fees are not restored on reload: return-fields.js adds those inputs on DOMContentLoaded, after the inline module has already restored localStorage, so the page silently recomputes with $2.50/$0.40 (Chromium: typed 5 -> $1,439.20; after reload field 2.5, $1,419.20)

In-house cost is one per-order rate held constant while the searched break-even re-prices the 3PL across volumes; the FAQ tells users to fold rent, software and labour into that rate, so in-house fixed costs are treated as variable and the break-even volume is biased (make-vs-buy needs fixed + variable on both sides)

Storage only per pallet: no bin/shelf/cubic-foot line or conversion, no peak-season surcharge, no account/per-SKU fees, minimum always applied to a subtotal that includes postage; pallets do not scale with volume in the sensitivity sweep
Orders-to-clear-minimum formula untested: a mutant dropping the storage and fixed-fee offset survived; tests only check the line exists
Same field has different defaults across engines: receivingPerUnit 0.12 in calculate vs 0.45 in inboundReceivingPerUnit; returnFee/restockFee 2.5/0.4 vs 3.5/4 in compareReturnDisposition
Inbound pallets and cartons billed fractionally (150 units / 60 = 2.5 pallets) instead of per whole container received
README Development command runs 2 of 9 test files; kitting page calls its defaults 'typical' without a source

verdict: A broad, private, well-tested browser calculator whose rate-card arithmetic is right: the default quote ($1,419.20, $14.19/order), searched break-even (345), the $2,500 minimum and its 187-order clearing volume, pallet/carton inbound conversion, aged storage, return disposition and kitting outputs all recompute by hand, every page carries the disclaimer, and 6 of 7 seeded bugs are caught. It misses the bar on correctness: when no break-even exists the summary, page and export all print '0 orders', the same figure shown when the 3PL wins at every volume, and custom return fees silently revert on reload. A fulfilment ops manager would also hit the model's limits within the hour: pallet-only storage (no bin or cubic-foot), no peak surcharge, minimums that always include postage, and an in-house side whose fixed costs are treated as per-order. Finished (completeness 3) but not at the senior-professional bar (correctness, fitness, domain and craft 2).
